problems.title: Count integers in a logarithm domain
problems.question: How many integers satisfy log₃(x−3)≤2?
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Require $0<x-3\le3^2$.
steps: Thus 3<x≤12. Integers 4 through 12 give nine solutions.

problems.title: An exponential with base less than one
problems.question: Solve (sin(π/9))^|x|>(sin(π/9))².
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: The base lies strictly between 0 and 1, so increasing the exponent decreases the value.
steps: Require |x|<2, giving −2<x<2.

problems.title: A cube-root logarithm base
problems.question: Solve log_(3/5)(x+7)<log_(cube-root(3/5))2.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
steps: The logarithm decreases, so x+7>8. This gives x>1 and automatically satisfies the argument domain x+7>0.

problems.title: A sphere centre’s distance to a section plane
problems.question: A radius-13 sphere contains three surface points at pairwise distances 6,8,10. Find centre-to-plane distance.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: The triangle is right with circumradius 5; $R^2=d^2+r^2$.
steps: The plane-section circle has radius 10/2=5. Thus d=√(169−25)=12.

problems.title: An insphere in a cone frustum
problems.question: A frustum has base radii 3,4 and slant height 7. Find its insphere radius.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Frustum height $h=\sqrt{l^2-(R-r)^2}$; an insphere tangent to both base planes has radius h/2.
steps: h=√(49−1)=4√3, so the sphere radius is 2√3. The axial trapezoid is tangential because its legs total 14 and bases total 6+8=14.

problems.title: A known solution determines whether the base is below one
problems.question: Solve log_a(2x−1)>log_a(x+7), knowing x=5 is a solution.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: At x=5 the arguments are 9 and 12, with 9<12. Thus the base must satisfy 0<a<1.
steps: The common argument domain is x>1/2. Reversing the comparison for a base below 1 gives 2x−1<x+7, so x<8.

problems.title: A variable logarithm base
problems.question: Solve log_x(6−x)≥2.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Domain x>0,x≠1,x<6; split into 0<x<1 and x>1.
steps: For 0<x<1, the comparison requires 6−x≤x², impossible in that interval.
For 1<x<6, it requires 6−x≥x², or (x+3)(x−2)≤0. The intersection is 1<x≤2.

problems.title: A radical inequality has an automatic negative-input part
problems.question: Find the sum of integer solutions of √(2x+3)≥x.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Domain x≥−3/2. For x≤0 the inequality is automatic; for x>0 square both sides.
steps: For positive x, 2x+3≥x² gives x≤3. Combined, the full solution interval is [−3/2,3].
Its integer members −1,0,1,2,3 sum to 5.

problems.title: Distance from a slanted segment to a cylinder axis
problems.question: A cylinder has height 6,radius 5. A length-10 segment joins points on opposite base circles. Find its shortest distance to the axis.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: The segment’s horizontal projection is a chord of length $\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=8$.
steps: Distance to the infinite vertical axis equals radial distance of the projection. The nearest projected point is the chord midpoint.
Its centre distance is √(5²−4²)=3.

problems.title: An inclined cone section with a quarter-circle chord
problems.question: A plane through a cone apex makes 45° with the base and cuts off a quarter of its base circumference. Cone height is 10. Find section area.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Chord central angle is 90°; apex height/chord distance from base centre =tan45°.
steps: The chord’s centre distance is 10. For a 90° chord this is R/√2, so R=10√2 and chord length=R√2=20.
The triangular section altitude is √(10²+10²)=10√2. Area=20×10√2/2=100√2.

problems.title: A nonnegative radical exceeds a negative expression
problems.question: Solve √(2^x−8)≥cosx−2.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: The radical requires x≥3; its value is then nonnegative, while cosx−2≤−1.
steps: Every point of the real domain satisfies the inequality. The solution set is [3,∞).

problems.title: A logarithm domain without an interior hole
problems.question: Which listed a makes log_(x+a)[(1−9x)/(x+15)] have a domain that is one nonempty open interval?
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Argument positivity gives x∈(−15,1/9); base conditions require x>−a and x≠1−a.
steps: For a=−7 or −5 the intersection is empty. For a=5,9,12 the excluded base-1 input lies inside the interval and splits it.
For a=18, x>−18 adds no restriction and x=−17 is already outside. The domain is exactly (−15,1/9).

problems.title: A radical endpoint can solve an inequality
problems.question: Count integer solutions of (x²−4x+3)√(9x−14−x²)≥0.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Radical domain is [2,7]; the polynomial is (x−1)(x−3).
steps: Inside (2,7), the radical is positive, so x≥3 is required. But at x=2 the radical is zero and the original product is also zero, so this isolated endpoint is valid.
The integer solutions are 2,3,4,5,6,7, totaling six.

problems.title: Volume ratio of an inscribed cylinder and prism
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has volume 9 and an inscribed cylinder. Which listed interval contains the cylinder volume?
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: For an equilateral base of inradius r, triangle area=3√3r² and circle area=πr².
steps: The equal-height volume ratio is π/(3√3). Cylinder volume=9π/(3√3)=√3π≈5.44, lying in (5,6).

problems.title: Circumsphere of a rectangular box
problems.question: A rectangular box has edges 4,6,12. Find circumsphere radius.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Radius is half the space diagonal.

problems.title: Compare increasing and decreasing functions
problems.question: Solve log₄(x+11)<7−x.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Domain x>−11; the left side strictly increases, the right strictly decreases.
steps: They are equal at x=5 because log₄16=2=7−5. Therefore the strict inequality holds precisely for −11<x<5.

problems.title: An exponential factor has a fixed sign
problems.question: Count integer roots of 3x+12·3^(√x)≥4x·3^(√x)+9.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Domain x≥0. Move terms and factor $(x-3)(3-4\cdot3^{\sqrt x})\ge0$.
steps: Since 3^(√x)≥1, the second factor is strictly negative. Thus x−3≤0.
The domain intersection is [0,3], containing integers 0,1,2,3.

problems.title: Two logarithms each have a simple lower bound
problems.question: Solve log₇(√(x−2)+7)·log₃(x²+x+3)≥2.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Domain x≥2; on it the first factor≥log₇7=1 and the second≥log₃9=2.
steps: Both factors are positive, so their product is at least 2 throughout the domain. Equality occurs at x=2.

problems.title: Circumsphere of an equal-edge pyramid
problems.question: Every lateral edge of a pyramid is 6 and its height is 3. Find its circumsphere volume.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: All base vertices have radius $\sqrt{6^2-3^2}=3\sqrt3$ about the altitude foot. The sphere centre lies on the altitude axis.
steps: Let its signed height above the base be z. Equal squared distances to apex and base vertices give (3−z)²=27+z².
Thus z=−3 and sphere radius=|3−(−3)|=6. Volume=4π·6³/3=288π.

problems.title: Insphere of a three-four-five cone
problems.question: A cone has base radius 3,height 4. Find its insphere radius.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: The axial triangle has base 6,altitude 4 and equal sides 5; its inradius is area/semiperimeter.
steps: Area=12,semiperimeter=(5+5+6)/2=8. The sphere radius equals the triangle inradius 12/8=1.5.

problems.title: Smallest and largest signed sum
problems.question: Multiply each member of {log₂2,log₂4,…,log₂64} by each member of {log₃9,log₃27,log₃81}, then independently choose a plus/minus sign for each of the 18 products. Find min and max absolute sums.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: The factor sets are {1,…,6} and {2,3,4}; their total product-sum is 21×9=189.
steps: All plus signs give maximum 189. Every signed sum has the same odd parity as 189, so its absolute value is at least 1.
This minimum is attainable: the six products with factor 4 sum to 84; add the product 5×2=10 to make 94. Give those seven terms minus signs and the other terms plus signs: 189−2×94=1.

problems.title: An odd root count in a symmetric system
problems.question: For which listed a does log₃(x+5)+y²=2, log₅(2x−3)−y⁴=a have an odd number of real solution pairs?
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Nonzero y solutions occur in ± pairs. An odd count requires y=0.
steps: At y=0 the first equation gives x=4, so the second gives a=log₅5=1.
To check sufficiency, put u=y²≥0. Then x=3^(2−u)−5 and a=log₅(2·3^(2−u)−13)−u² on its domain. This expression strictly decreases with u from 1 at u=0.
Thus a=1 has only u=0 and exactly one solution pair (4,0).

problems.title: Area under a line after a variable-base logarithm
problems.question: Find the shaded area satisfying log_(0.8−|x|)(x²+1)≥log_(0.8−|x|)(9−2x), y≤5x,y²≤16.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: The base requires |x|<0.8 and is below 1. Reverse the logarithmic argument comparison.
steps: The logarithmic inequality becomes x²+1≤9−2x, or −4≤x≤2, automatically true on (−0.8,0.8). Both arguments are positive there.
The other bounds give −4≤y≤5x. The region is a triangle, with limiting base length 1.6 and height 8. Open vertical endpoints do not change its area.

problems.title: Rotate a right trapezoid around its shorter base
problems.question: A right trapezoid has bases 10,8 and area 36. Rotate it around the shorter base. Find volume.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Height=area/midline=36/9=4; use a full cylinder minus the missing cone.
steps: The rotated body is a radius-4,length-10 cylinder with a radius-4,height-2 cone removed from the overhang end.

problems.title: External tetrahedron-face apexes on one sphere
problems.question: On every face of regular tetrahedron ABCD, build an external regular pyramid whose apex lies on its circumsphere; call the apexes D₁,C₁,B₁,A₁ opposite D,C,B,A. Find the angle between ABC₁ and ACD₁.
problems.idea: Write every domain restriction first, then apply the logarithmic or geometric relation.
formulas: Use a centred regular tetrahedron A=(1,1,1),B=(1,−1,−1),C=(−1,1,−1),D=(−1,−1,1).
steps: For each face, its external regular-pyramid apex on the sphere is the antipode of the opposite original vertex. Thus C₁=−C=(1,−1,1),D₁=−D=(1,1,−1).
Plane ABC₁ is x=1 and plane ACD₁ is y=1. These coordinate planes are perpendicular.
